name: profiles_are_read_first
why: THE OPERATION THAT THE CATALOGUE ASKED FOR AND THAT WAS NOT THERE. `structural_member` and `rectangular_frame` say, in their own description, «FIRST CALL weldment_profiles and copy profile_path and configuration FROM THERE TO THE LETTER». That name appeared four times in the catalogue -- all four inside the text of whoever asked for it -- and zero times among the executable names: the model read an instruction that led nowhere, and the only thing it could do was invent a path and a size.
_why_making_up_the_measurement_gives_no_: It is written in the comment of `WeldmentOperations` from before this case: if the size is not there, SOLIDWORKS does not fail -- it uses the active configuration of the profile. The part comes out with a wall different from the confirmed one, the rebuild is clean, and nobody notices until the shop floor. A check that catches it already exists, and it is good, but it can fire only AFTER someone has guessed. This case proves that now there is nothing left to guess.
_and_this_case_went_red_twice_for_the_sa: First with `segments: [[[0,0],[600,0]]]`, nested arrays: «Segment 1 is not readable». Then with `[{"start":[0,0],"end":[600,0]}]`, objects but with two coordinates: «At segment 1 the point start does not have three coordinates». The true format is a list of objects with points of THREE absolute coordinates in mm: `[{"start":[0,0,0],"end":[600,0,0]}]`. Both times the format was INVENTED instead of read in `SegmentsFrom` -- which is exactly the defect this case tells about, repeated twice while it was being written. It is kept written here because reading two bench errors costs more than twenty lines of source.
_why_the_numbers_are_not_written_here: Which profiles exist depends on the library of this installation, not on the code: writing «there are 37 profiles» would mean a case that goes red when someone adds a tube. Instead we require that the list is NOT EMPTY, that every entry carries a whole path, and -- the line that counts -- that a size taken from there and copied into `structural_member` is accepted.

expect.why: the square tube is one file only: if two came out, «search» would not be filtering
THE PATH IS GIVEN WHOLE. It is what `structural_member` wants in «profile_path», and rebuilding it from name and folder is the way to get it wrong.
THE SIZE WRITTEN AS IT MUST BE COPIED. «80X80X5» with capital X: that is how it is in the file, and «80x80x5» would be something else that SOLIDWORKS would ignore without saying.
the warning travels with the answer, not only in the catalogue: whoever reads this answer may never have read the description of the operation
THE CIRCLE CLOSES HERE. The size read at step 1 and copied at step 2 builds the bar: it is the proof that the two pieces of the catalogue now really talk to each other, not just quote each other.

expect._why_the_number_is_not_the_one_from_the_: The formula (80*80 - 70*70) * 600 gives 900,000 mm3, and the real part makes 881,973.4 -- eighteen thousand less. It is not an error: a structural tube has CORNER FILLETS, inside and outside, and the formula assumes sharp edges. The first run of this case came out red exactly like this, with 881,973 against 900,000 expected: the expected number had been COMPUTED instead of measured. Now the centre is the measurement and the formula is written here beside it to remember by how much it is wrong.
expect.tolerance_why: 500 mm3 is 0.06%: it covers the rebuild noise and a slightly different corner radius on another profile of the library. It still discriminates very widely: the wrong size CLOSEST -- 70x70x5 -- would give about 780,000, that is a hundred thousand mm3 away. An 80x80x4 would give about 715,000.
